facts.statement: Only one species, Craspedodon lonzeensis, is known from the genus Craspedodon.
facts.quote: Only a single species, C. lonzeensis, is known.

facts.statement: Belgian paleontologist Louis Dollo described the herbivorous dinosaur Craspedodon lonzeensis in 1883.
facts.quote: In 1883 Belgian paleontologist Louis Dollo described the fauna found in the Late Cretaceous of Belgium near Lonzée, naming the theropod species Megalosaurus lonzeensis and the new herbivorous dinosaur Craspedodon lonzeensis.

facts.statement: The genus was identified based on three teeth found in the Lonzée Member that showed similarities to Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Dollo identified Craspedodon from three teeth in the collections of the Museum of Natural Sciences in Brussels, from the Lonzée Member, finding the most similarities with species of Iguanodon amongst ornithischians.

facts.statement: The age of the Lonzée Member, where the fossils were found, is now understood to be from the Coniacian to Santonian stages.
facts.quote: Dollo specified the Lonzée Member as being middle Senonian in age, which is now understood to be Coniacian to Santonian.

facts.statement: Craspedodon was originally classified as an ornithopod related to Iguanodon, but this view was revisited in 2007 by Godefroit and Lambert.
facts.quote: Since its description, Craspedodon was considered an ornithopod following the relationship with Iguanodon suggested by Dollo, but this was revisited in 2007 by Belgian paleontologists Pascal Godefroit and Olivier Lambert.

facts.statement: Researchers were unable to determine if Craspedodon is a valid diagnostic taxon or a nomen dubium because tooth anatomy is too poorly understood.
facts.quote: They were unable to determine whether Craspedodon was a diagnostic taxon or a nomen dubium, identifying some features that suggest separation but also noting that tooth anatomy is too poorly understood to be definitive.

facts.statement: Godefroit and Lambert suggested Craspedodon was a neoceratopsian closer to Ceratopsoidea than Protoceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Craspedodon was long thought to be an iguanodontian, but Godefroit & Lambert (2007) suggested that it was actually a neoceratopsian, perhaps closer to Ceratopsoidea than Protoceratopsidae.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Craspedodon might instead represent a hadrosauroid ornithopod.
facts.quote: However, the describers of Ajkaceratops noted that Craspedodon might instead represent a hadrosauroid ornithopod.

facts.statement: Craspedodon lonzeensis lived approximately 85 million years ago during the Santonian stage in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Craspedodon lonzeensis es la única especie conocida del género dudoso extinto Craspedodon (gr. “diente con borde”) de dinosaurio neornistisquio posiblemente un ceratopsiano, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico hace aproximadamente 85 millones de años, en el Santoniense, en lo que es hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The species is known only from three teeth found in Belgium that are similar to those of Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Conocido por solo tres dientes encontrados en Bélgica, similar a los de Iguanodon.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, IRSNB R59, is the smallest of the three teeth.
facts.quote: El holotipo, IRSNB R59, es el diente más pequeño.

facts.statement: A 2007 study cautiously concluded that the tooth shape, ridge length, and thickened base might indicate membership in Neoceratopsia, specifically basal Ceratopsoidea.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio de 2007 concluyó con mucha cautela que, dada la forma del plano de corte, la longitud de las crestas dentales y la base del diente engrosada podría ser un miembro de Neoceratopsia y más específicamente una especie basal en el Ceratopsoidea.

facts.statement: It is believed Craspedodon arrived in Europe via land bridges connecting the continent to Asia during the Aptian period, rather than from North America.
facts.quote: Se cree que llegó a Europa a través de puentes de tierra que unieron este continente durante el periodo Aptiano con Asia; un origen de América del Norte fue rechazado.

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Craspedodon as Iguanodontoidea.
The time range for Craspedodon is estimated from 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Santonian (89.8 to 83.6 million years ago)
